content:
We need to search templates for each step. Steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated acid (the double bond). 3) amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine). The target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We need retrosynthesis: break into three precursors.

First retrosynthetic disconnections: The sulfonamide linking the tolyl sulfonyl group to the phenyl ring. So we can disconnect the S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and an aniline. The other part is the aryl sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide side chain.

Second: The amide bond between the unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So break C-N amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline.

Third: The α,β-unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with para substituent). So break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid precursor is the aldehyde (c2ccc(... )cc2) with aldehyde at position where the double bond attaches. So we need to identify the aldehyde: the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl group has a side chain /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde would be c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So we can propose that.

Thus final three precursors: (1) p-toluidine (or tolyl amine) for sulfonamide formation? Actually sulfonamide formation: we need sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (the phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide side chain). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the tolyl ring (the first phenyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (first phenyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So sulfonamide formation could be between aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride). So we need two fragments: (A) 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) and (B) 4-(α,β-unsaturated amide phenyl) sulfonyl chloride.

Thus step 1 retrosynthesis: disconnect S-N bond to give p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). Step 2: disconnect amide bond to give α,β-unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step 3: disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (or malonic acid derivative). So final precursors: p-toluidine, 4-(aldehyde phenyl) sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride contains the aldehyde? Actually after step 2, the sulfonyl chloride fragment still contains the unsaturated acid side chain attached to phenyl. After step 2, we have sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl which has side chain unsaturated acid (C=CH-COOH). So step 3 will convert that unsaturated acid to aldehyde? Actually the unsaturated acid is part of the sulfonyl chloride fragment. The Doebner modification would be applied to that phenyl ring to create the unsaturated acid from aldehyde. So the sulfonyl chloride fragment after step 2 is: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 with side chain /C=C/COOH (unsaturated acid). So step 3: break that side chain to aldehyde: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2-CHO.

Thus final three precursors: (1) p-toluidine (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1). (2) 4-(aldehyde phenyl)sulfonyl chloride (SMILES: O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C=O)cc1). (3) aniline (c3ccccc3N) for amide formation? Wait the amide formation uses aniline as nucleophile to react with the unsaturated acid to give amide. So we need aniline as second amine. So we have three precursors: p-toluidine, 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride, aniline.

But we also need malonic acid for Doebner? In retrosynthesis we break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid, but malonic acid is a reagent not part of final route? The route must have 3 reactions, so we need three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation, 2) amide coupling, 3) Doebner modification. The Doebner uses aldehyde + malonic acid to give unsaturated acid. So malonic acid is a reagent, not a precursor in the final route? The route representation expects each reaction node with children being precursors (reactants). So for Doebner step, children would be aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So we need to include malonic acid as a precursor.

Thus total precursors: p-toluidine, aniline, 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride, malonic acid.

But the route must have 3 reactions, each reaction node with children being reactants. So we need hierarchical tree: root molecule (target). Its children: reaction 1 (sulfonamide formation) producing target from two fragments: (a) sulfonyl chloride fragment (which itself is product of reaction 2?) Actually we need to order steps: forward synthesis: first Doebner to make unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride; second amide coupling to attach aniline; third sulfonamide formation to attach p-toluidine. So retrosynthesis: break target into sulfonamide step: gives sulfonyl chloride fragment (with unsaturated acid) and p-toluidine. Then break sulfonyl chloride fragment via amide step? Wait amide step is on the unsaturated acid side chain, not on sulfonyl chloride. The sulfonyl chloride fragment still contains unsaturated acid; we need to break amide bond to give unsaturated acid and aniline. So the sulfonyl chloride fragment is product of amide step? Actually amide step yields sulfonyl chloride fragment with unsaturated acid attached to aniline? Wait the amide step forms the amide between unsaturated acid and aniline, producing the side chain attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So after amide step, we have sulfonyl chloride fragment with unsaturated amide attached. So in retrosynthesis, we break that amide to give unsaturated acid (still attached to sulfonyl chloride) and aniline. So the unsaturated acid fragment is then broken via Doebner to aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus tree:

Root: target molecule (type mol, smiles target)
children: reaction node (sulfonamide formation) template_id X, children: mol1 = p-toluidine, mol2 = intermediate A (the sulfonyl chloride fragment with unsaturated amide). That intermediate A is a molecule node.

Intermediate A node children: reaction node (amide coupling) template_id Y, children: mol3 = aniline, mol4 = intermediate B (unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl chloride).

Intermediate B node children: reaction node (Doebner) template_id Z, children: mol5 = aldehyde (aryl-CHO sulfonyl chloride), mol6 = malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH).

Thus we need template IDs for each reaction type. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

Let's search for sulfonamide formation template.
